statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Investia Egypt — the official digital platform of the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) at https://www.investia.gov.eg; name clearance is integrated in the 'Company Establishment' pre-approval flow. statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory name must be registered in Arabic script using the official Arabic language (the public/legal name). A Latin-script transliteration may be filed for operational/tax invoice purposes if it appears as a secondary denomination in the Articles of Association, but the Arabic name is the legally operative name in the Egyptian Commercial Registry. The proposed name must start with a distinctive token and end with the legal form; 'LLC' or 'Limited Liability Company' renders as 'ش.م.م' (Sharika Thabat al-Mas'ooliyya al-Mahdooda). The name must not contradict public order, must not be misleading, and must not convey false government sponsorship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon GAFI rejection, the applicant shall file a written administrative appeal to the GAFI Legal Affairs Department within 30 days from the rejection notice, providing a fresh Arabic name proposal and supporting clearance from the sectoral regulator (if the rejection relates to a sensitive token). If GAFI does not respond within 15 working days, or upon an adverse decision, the applicant may file an appeal before the Administrative Court (Qada' al-Istithna') via the Council of State within 60 days from the date of the adverse decision, pursuant to Law No. 106 of 2018; in parallel, the applicant may simultaneously reserve one alternative name through the Investia portal to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a primary registered address for an Egyptian LLC. Law No. 159 of 1981 and the Commercial Registry regulations require a physical, rentable Egyptian address (office or commercial premises) under lease or ownership, which must be verifiable by the tax authority and the Commercial Registry; a virtual mailbox may be used only as a supplementary correspondence address. The registered office must be located inside Egypt; if the facility is used, it must be present to permit physical access for audits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderately high — unannounced physical on-site inspections by the insolvency/registry auditor and the tax authority (Egyptian Tax Authority) occur in approximately 35–50% of newly established LLCs within the first 12 months where the registered office is a single-tenant unit or addresses that appear virtual; the risk rises substantially (75%+) if the declared office is in a residential flat with no business evidence or is listed without a real lease. For this Licensing Marketplace (ISIC 5920 / NAICS 512240), GAFI expects demonstrable operational substance (lease, equipment, records, staff) at the registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Central Department of Taxpayer Registration; official portal: www.eta.gov.eg; electronic invoicing/fiscal clearance portal: inov.eta.gov.eg; Suez Canal Economic Zone tax units operate under ETA supervision.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Egyptian LLC: (1) complete company incorporation and commercial registration with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) or competent commercial registry; (2) file Tax Card (TIN) application with ETA Taxpayer Registration Department presenting the incorporation certificate, authenticated Memorandum/Articles of Association (foreign consular attestation required if executed abroad), lease deed or address proof, legal entity data form, notarized board resolutions, and passport copies/POA of foreign managers; (3) obtain the unified Tax Card/TIN; (4) register for VAT within 30 days after taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000; (5) enroll in the ETA e-invoicing portal and create a machine-readable API credential for authorized signers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — An Egyptian LLC is a resident tax entity subject to corporate income tax (CIT) at 22.5% on worldwide income (Law 91/2005 as amended); no pass-through treatment for members; foreign shareholders' distributions are subject to dividend withholding tax at 10% unless reduced by treaty; profits attributable to a foreign permanent establishment may be exempt under treaty conditions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' regime exists. Available elections: (a) voluntary VAT registration before reaching the EGP 500,000 threshold; (b) election for annual VAT filing with monthly prepayments; (c) election to apply reduced treaty withholding rates on royalties/licensing fees remitted to non-residents (domestic WHT on royalties is 20%; treaty rates generally 0–15% depending on jurisdiction); (d) election for simplified transfer-pricing documentation (summary file) where related-party transactions are below EGP 8 million per counterparty per fiscal year; (e) election to consolidate multiple foreign-source service contracts under a single exported-services zero-rating file.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended (replacing GST Law 11/1991), extended to Suez Canal Economic Zone special economic status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies of goods and services; mandatory registration within 30 days of crossing the threshold; non-resident suppliers supplying digital services to final Egyptian consumers are required to register via a fiscal representative or direct ETA enrollment regardless of threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory fiscal clearance in real time: all VAT-registered taxpayers must integrate billing/ERP systems with the ETA e-invoicing platform using REST API (JSON), transmit invoice XML/JSON for pre-clearance, obtain a 2048-bit RSA digital signature and QR code containing the Unique Invoice Identifier; e-receipts are mandatory for B2C retail. Invoices without ETA clearance are legally invalid, non-deductible, and subject to penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 31 of VAT Law 67/2016 zero-rates exported goods and services. For royalty-free stock music licensing by an Egyptian LLC: (a) the LLC must be VAT-registered; (b) the license must be granted to a non-resident licensee or digital marketplace acting for non-resident end-users; (c) the economic benefit and consumers of the licensed music must be located outside Egypt; (d) the license fee must be arm's length and received in convertible foreign currency; (e) the export must be evidenced by licensing contracts, distribution platform statements, and bank inward remittance records. Electronic services delivered to non-residents are treated as exported services eligible for 0% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (goods) or ETA electronic service-export notification (intangible/digital services)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / digital delivery log with foreign IP-address usage records for online music delivery
Inward Remittance Certificate from an Egyptian bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Licensing agreement or sublicense agreement with the non-resident licensee/platform
VAT invoice bearing the ETA e-invoice QR code and zero-rated export code
Non-resident status confirmation, economic-destination declaration, and beneficial owner self-certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA audits export zero-rating claims against CBE bank records, platform payout data, and licensee due-diligence files. Failure to remit export proceeds to Egypt within 180 days triggers retrospective VAT clawback at 14% on the full invoice value plus late-remittance late-payment interest of 2% per month under VAT Law Articles 66 and 68. Fraudulent zero-rating or false documentation constitutes tax evasion punishable by a fine of 25%–100% of the evaded tax, imprisonment for not less than six months, suspension of the Tax Card and e-invoicing clearance credentials, disgorgement of VAT refunds, and joint liability of directors/managers under Article 72.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the exclusive monetary and foreign exchange authority under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Banking and Banking System Law), acting jointly with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) for capital account entry/exit and repatriation registration, and with the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) for remittance tax clearance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a de facto freely floating EGP regime following the CBE full liberalization of 6 March 2024. Current-account transactions — royalties, licensing fees, sound-recording exports, and service invoices — are fully convertible for bona fide business purposes when supported by commercial contracts, VAT invoices, and the accepting bank's Balance of Payments declaration. Capital-account transactions, principally foreign equity injections into the Egyptian LLC, are convertible but administratively controlled: the inward remittance must be cleared through an authorized bank, credited to an investment account, and registered in the GAFI investment file in order to perfect the legal right to future profit and liquidation proceeds repatriation. Practical profit remittance hurdles are documentary rather than prohibitive: the bank requires audited financial statements, ETA final corporate income tax clearance, proof that applicable dividend withholding or treaty relief has been settled, and CBE/GAFI remittance filings; during episodes of FX liquidity stress, the conversion queue can temporarily delay EGP funding and offshore payouts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE exchange control instructions, and as amended after the 6 March 2024 float, Egyptian exporters — including the LLC benefiting from digital audio licensing revenue: (i) must repatriate the full export proceeds into an Egyptian authorized bank within 90 days from the shipment date, service completion date, or the contractual billing milestone; (ii) may request bank-approved extension for deferred-payment commercial agreements; and (iii) are subject to no mandatory conversion ratio under the current regime — proceeds may be retained in USD/EUR accounts and converted voluntarily at interbank rates. The receiving bank must record the service-export declaration and evidence of underlying license receipts in the CBE reporting system; overdue unrepatriated amounts are flagged as exchange-control breaches and can trigger suspension of an exporter's banking facilities.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a treasury collection sub-channel, Low as a substitute for an Egyptian banking relationship. Egypt does not grant generic electronic-money licences to offshore EMI firms; EMIs cannot operate local EGP-denominated corporate accounts and are not CBE-supervised. Offshore EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Currenxie, and similar facilitators) may lawfully aggregate Stripe/PayPal marketplace payouts and re-credit the LLC's Egyptian bank account via SWIFT MT103, provided each end-buyer licence invoice is reconciled and the Egyptian bank accepts the EMI as the original remitter. However, the CBE subjects aggregated transfers to enhanced AML review because the ultimate payers are not self-evident, and EMIs cannot perform EGP conversion or onshore clearing without passing through a licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person mandate: High. Egyptian banks require the LLC's legal representative to appear physically at the branch for corporate account opening, accompanied by the Commercial Registry certificate, tax card, VAT registration certificate, constitutional documents, board resolution appointing authorized signatories, and UBO declarations. Remote video onboarding is not a standard substitute for an LLC; CBE e-KYC applies mainly to low-risk natural persons and payments accounts. A non-resident director may instead execute a notarized and Egypt-consular legalized power of attorney in favour of a local signatory, but the bank will still request passport copies, source-of-wealth statements, and sanctions screening for every beneficial owner holding at least 25% of the LLC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume marketplace payouts (aggregated Stripe/PayPal remittances) presented as single incoming MT103 injections, preventing the bank from mapping proceeds to named end-user licensees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly reconciliation pack comprising marketplace payout reports, per-license royalty schedules by buyer legal entity and licence key, executed licence order snapshots, VAT e-invoices for net aggregates, end-customer jurisdiction lists, and a board resolution confirming IFRS 15 royalty recognition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible-export KYC mismatch: bank classification forms default to physical goods exports while the licence (ISIC 5920) is delivered by download, so no customs declaration or bill of lading is producible.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Master Licence Agreement and standard click-wrap licence terms, delivery-platform audit logs evidencing server-side fulfilment, Balance of Payments classification as 'charges for the use of intellectual property', CBE service-export declaration, SOC 2 attestation for the distribution platform, and NAFEZA or foreign-trade system export reference where the bank requires one.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty stripping or undisclosed related parties: non-resident shareholders and beneficial owners receiving future dividends or management fees from the Egyptian LLC trigger transfer-pricing and dividend-repatriation scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder register with UBO percentages, GAFI investment registration and original FDI capital certificates, board minutes approving profit appropriation, audited financial statements, ETA corporate income tax filing and tax clearance certificate, Egyptian transfer pricing local file with comparability analysis for audio licensing, and CBE profit-remittance application forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity of offshore wallets: payments initiated from EMI balances rather than from the actual licensee account create unverifiable fund provenance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Principal-to-principal contracts with Stripe/PayPal and each EMI, KYC/KYB questionnaires for wallet holders, payout trail from each licensee to the Egyptian bank account, negative-match results on OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening, internal AML policy and risk assessment prepared by the compliance officer, and CBE anti-money laundering filings under Law No. 80 of 2002 and its executive regulations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the foreign shareholder initiates a SWIFT MT103 with field 70 identifying 'Foreign Direct Investment — equity subscription in an Egyptian LLC', destined for the CBE-registered capital account at the Egyptian bank; the recipient bank obtains the GAFI project file and the signed constitutional documentation, credits the USD/EUR capital account or converts into EGP at the interbank rate, issues an investment deposit certificate, and records the investment in the CBE/GAFI system. Foreign-currency equity injection is the standard route for creating the registered foreign investment position; an EGP-denominated injection from abroad is not recognized for GAFI repatriation rights. The LLC must notify the bank of any beneficial-ownership change and maintain the investment file with GAFI's investor support centre.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 transfers for recurring royalty, distributor, and vendor payments, each supported by ETA tax clearance, VAT invoices, and CBE foreign-payment declarations; (ii) commercial letters of credit and documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for physical-media distribution, master-recording acquisitions, and equipment purchases requiring trade finance; (iii) Egyptian interbank EGP settlements through the national RTGS system for payroll and local operating expenses; and (iv) dividend and profit remittances through the bank's remittance desk after GAFI and ETA clearance, with treaty-relief documentation when applicable. All outbound transfers require positive sanctions screening and matching of the underlying commercial document set.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/EGP forward contracts with an authorized CBE bank, exercisable against genuine commercial exposure and maturities up to 365 days, valued against the CBE published fixing.
Onshore USD/EGP currency swaps combining spot and forward legs for working-capital liquidity conversion.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed by the foreign parent or offshore banking counterparty referencing the EGP interbank rate, as NDFs are not negotiable inside the Egyptian banking book.
FX options for hedging forecast royalty receivables, subject to internal credit approval and documented underlying trade exposure under CBE derivatives authorizations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 41) together with audited financial statements and tax reconciliation attachments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Income Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year-end; calendar-year taxpayers must file by 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 2% per month on unsettled corporate income tax; delinquent return may trigger estimated assessment, administrative fine up to EGP 50,000, bank attachment, and criminal referral for persistent non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry annual renewal declaration and annual fee payment, including updated statement of registered particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Bureau, Ministry of Trade and Industry (governorate registrar where the LLC's seat is registered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During January of each calendar year with reference to the LLC's registration certificate anniversary; late window may run through February before fines accrue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily late fines for non-payment; continued default leads to temporary suspension of the registered company's legal status and ultimately administrative strike-off from the Commercial Registry after statutory warning and 30-day grace period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll and social insurance contribution declaration (Form 62) and wage reconciliation statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Organisation for Social Insurance (NOSI) – Office of the Governorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March of the calendar year following the contribution period; advance monthly declarations must be filed by the 15th of each month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Collection penalties equivalent to 10% of unpaid contributions and accrual of monthly interest; unpaid contributions may be collected as tax arrears and may lead to administrative restrictions on commercial registration renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minutes of the annual shareholders' meeting approving the financial statements, retained as part of the company's corporate book records and demonstrated upon request to the registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones) / Commercial Registry inspection on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., by 30 June for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting or record minutes renders directors liable to shareholders and may be treated as a deficiency in corporate governance during inspection, potentially leading to a compliance order and administrative penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No turnover threshold: every Egyptian limited liability company (LLC) is required by the Companies Law to appoint one or more licensed public accountants as auditors; annual audit is mandatory regardless of revenue or asset size for LLCs under the Egyptian income tax and companies legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) as issued by the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA), which are substantially aligned with IFRS; group entities or investment-law companies may use IFRS where the parent bank or lenders so require, subject to ETA acceptance for tax purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Egypt's Anti-Money Laundering Law (Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended) and the Cabinet Decision on Beneficial Ownership Registration, the LLC must maintain a beneficial ownership register and file the UBO update through the ETA/GAFI digital registry whenever there is any change in direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more; an annual confirmation update must be submitted during the annual commercial registry renewal window, covering all share transfers, pledge, or control changes during the prior calendar year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400–900 per annum for registered office and professional corporate secretarial-services provider in major governorates (Cairo, Giza, Alexandria)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 700–1,800 per annum for a licensed Egyptian auditor for a small-to-medium licensing LLC with simple transactions and cross-border royalty income

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% of net taxable profits for most companies under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holiday or preferential deduction is identified for an ordinary commercial soundscape or audio-sample licensing business. Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 can provide a deduction from taxable net profits equal to 30% or 50% of qualifying investment costs for eligible projects and locations, subject to statutory conditions, a maximum deduction of 80% of paid-up capital, and a deduction period not exceeding seven years. Eligibility requires project-specific confirmation; the activity description alone does not establish entitlement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual corporate income tax return for legal persons, commonly designated Form 101, filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal. Confirm the currently enabled form and applicable portal workflow with ETA because electronic forms and procedures may change.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; tax is generally paid through advance payments during the year, subject to applicable statutory rules and reconciliation on filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within four months after the end of the tax period. A company using a calendar-year tax period generally files by 30 April. The tax period and any approved non-calendar accounting period should be verified against the company’s tax registration and records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the company’s ETA tax registration number, legal name, address, legal form, activity, and tax period exactly as registered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder does not replace the Egyptian LLC as the taxpayer. Report the Egyptian entity’s own registration details; identify foreign related parties in the relevant related-party disclosures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report profit or loss per financial statements prepared under applicable Egyptian accounting and statutory requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Egyptian company’s results, not the non-resident owner’s worldwide income. Maintain source records for cross-border income and expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting results to taxable income, including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, depreciation differences, provisions, and other adjustments required by law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Egyptian deductibility, withholding, and transfer-pricing rules to payments to non-residents. Retain contracts, invoices, evidence of services, and proof of withholding and remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after allowable deductions and available loss relief, then apply the applicable corporate tax rate and credit eligible tax payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only losses attributable to the Egyptian taxpayer and supported by filed returns and records. Do not assume foreign tax credits or treaty relief without satisfying statutory documentation and eligibility requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose related-party transactions and complete the applicable transfer-pricing sections or attachments required by the current return and ETA procedures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the foreign counterparty, transaction type, amount, pricing basis, and supporting documentation. Apply the arm’s-length principle to cross-border dealings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report applicable withholding taxes, advance payments, and other credits or payments in the relevant return fields and schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian payer should report and remit withholding on payments to non-residents where required. Treaty relief should be supported by valid residence and beneficial-ownership documentation and accepted procedures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete the required declaration and submit through the ETA system by the statutory deadline; retain the submission receipt and payment evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company’s authorized representative or registered tax agent should ensure valid electronic credentials, timely submission, and retention of the filed return and supporting records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing can attract penalties under the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 206 of 2020, including fines generally ranging from EGP 3,000 to EGP 50,000 for specified return-filing violations, with higher consequences for repeated violations where statutory conditions apply. Late payment can trigger additional tax calculated under the law, generally by reference to the Central Bank of Egypt credit-and-discount rate plus the statutory margin, for each month or part of a month. Understatements, evasion, and failure to withhold or remit can produce separate assessments, additional tax, fines, and criminal exposure. Confirm the current rate, penalty classification, and procedural notice applicable to the specific violation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Generally 10% withholding tax on dividends paid by an Egyptian resident company, subject to statutory exemptions, qualifying listed-share treatment, and any applicable treaty reduction. The domestic rate and a treaty rate must be assessed against the shareholder’s status, holding, beneficial ownership, and treaty eligibility.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, identify the recipient’s residence, beneficial ownership, and applicable Egyptian double tax agreement. Obtain a current tax residence certificate from the recipient’s competent authority and the treaty forms and supporting documents required by ETA; provide them to the Egyptian payer and retain them with the payment file. Apply a reduced rate only where the treaty conditions and administrative requirements are met; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate. Treaty claims, refunds, and advance approvals depend on the applicable treaty and ETA procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic withholding on specified payments to non-residents, including royalties and interest, is generally 20% of the gross payment under Egyptian income tax rules, subject to statutory exclusions and treaty relief. The applicable treaty may reduce or cap the rate and may distinguish royalties, interest, equipment leasing, software, or technical services. Classify audio licences, downloadable content, platform access, and related services by their actual contractual rights and applicable treaty definitions; do not assume a royalty rate solely from the commercial label.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Egyptian rules require arm’s-length pricing and transfer-pricing documentation for controlled transactions. The commonly applied local-file materiality threshold is EGP 8 million of aggregate related-party transactions in a tax period; a master file is generally relevant where the multinational group’s consolidated revenue reaches EGP 3 billion. These thresholds and filing obligations should be verified against current ETA rules and guidance for the relevant tax year. Country-by-country reporting may apply separately to qualifying multinational groups, including the applicable consolidated-revenue threshold and reporting-entity rules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not have a general-purpose Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to that of certain offshore jurisdictions. Egyptian tax, company, beneficial-ownership, anti-avoidance, and treaty rules nevertheless require genuine transactions, arm’s-length terms, accurate accounting, and support for the commercial purpose and performance of cross-border services and licensing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing income, fabricating expenses, keeping false books, materially misstating taxable income, or deliberately failing to file or pay tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid tax and additional tax, administrative fines, and criminal prosecution under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 and Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 206 of 2020. Criminal fines and imprisonment depend on the offense, intent, amount, and applicable statutory provisions; obtain case-specific advice before quantifying exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face personal criminal liability where they participate in, authorize, or knowingly facilitate an offense. Corporate status does not shield an individual from liability for personal conduct. Civil recovery is generally against the taxpayer, subject to statutory rules governing responsible persons and enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold or remit tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying non-resident royalties, interest, dividends, or other taxable amounts without applying required withholding, filing required statements, or remitting withheld amounts on time.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Egyptian payer may be assessed the unwithheld tax, additional tax, and applicable fines; intentional conduct may trigger criminal consequences. Treaty relief does not excuse withholding where eligibility or documentation requirements are unmet.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers may face personal exposure for knowing or intentional participation and under applicable enforcement provisions. No automatic director liability or travel ban should be assumed without a specific statutory basis or court or enforcement order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party licences, services, funding, or intellectual-property transactions outside the arm’s-length range; failing to maintain required documentation; or submitting inaccurate related-party disclosures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may adjust taxable profits and assess additional tax, interest or additional tax, and applicable penalties. Documentation failures can increase audit and penalty exposure; the amount depends on the applicable provision and facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company is ordinarily the primary taxpayer. Directors or officers may face individual liability where they knowingly participate in fraud, false declarations, or another offense; a transfer-pricing adjustment alone does not automatically pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unsubstantiated royalty-free or below-market related-party licensing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing or receiving music, sound recordings, samples, or platform rights without a written agreement, demonstrable rights ownership, commercial rationale, or arm’s-length support, particularly between related parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible denial or adjustment of deductions, taxable-profit reallocation, withholding-tax reassessment, and penalties for inaccurate returns or transfer-pricing non-compliance. Copyright infringement may also create separate civil or criminal exposure under applicable intellectual-property law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for knowing infringement, fraud, or other personal misconduct. Ordinary tax adjustments or company copyright liability do not, without more, automatically create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the LLC to conceal beneficial ownership, disguise the source or destination of funds, process criminal proceeds, or submit false corporate or banking information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential account restrictions, tax and regulatory investigations, asset restraint or confiscation, administrative sanctions, and criminal prosecution under applicable anti-money-laundering and company laws. Penalties depend on the conduct and governing statute.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly participate may face personal criminal and civil consequences. Travel restrictions or imprisonment require an applicable legal basis and competent authority action; they are not automatic consequences of a tax filing failure.
